newsitem.title: HONG KONG: China Weifu plans 42 mln new B shares.
newsitem.headline: China Weifu plans 42 mln new B shares.

text.p: Jiangsu-based automobile parts maker Weifu Fuel Injection Co Ltd said on Wednesday it planned to offer up to 42 million new B shares and use the proceeds to upgrade its technology and set up joint-ventures.

The fund-raising plan was approved on February 16 by 291 shareholders representing 70.52 percent of Weifu's outstanding shares, the company said in a statement in Wednesday's Shenzhen-based Securities Times.
The time and precise scale of the offer, which needs approval of securities authorities, have yet to be fixed, the company said without elaborating.
Weifu's total share capital of 183.4355 million shares consists of 68 million B shares, 92.4355 million state shares, eight million legal person shares and 15 million staff shares.
A company spokesman earlier told the Hong Kong-based newsletter China Securities Bulletin that the firm had unaudited net profits of 66.5 million yuan in 1996 due to strong sales.
Weifu expects net profits to grow 10-to-15 percent year-on-year in 1997 in anticipation of robust demand, the spokesman said.
The company posted post-tax profit of 62.98 million yuan for 1995 versus 53.37 million yuan in 1994 under international accounting standards.
The spokesman said in 1996, the company received purchase orders of 800 million yuan, with most for delivery this year.
Weifu's 1996 half-year net was 33.2 million yuan, up 13.07 percent from 29.37 million yuan in the 1995 period, under international accounting standards.
